name: FOLLICLE STIMULATING HORMONE
description: Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH) measures pituitary gonadotropin function and evaluates reproductive endocrine status. This test assesses ovarian reserve, menopause, hypogonadism, and pituitary disorders affecting FSH secretion.

testdeatils.instrumentation: Abbott Architect, Roche Elecsys, Beckman Coulter

literatureReview: Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH) is a pituitary gonadotropin that regulates gametogenesis. In women, levels vary by cycle phase: follicular 3-12 mIU/mL, ovulatory 6-17 mIU/mL, luteal 1-9 mIU/mL. Postmenopausal levels rise to 25-135 mIU/mL. In men, normal range is 1.4-15.4 mIU/mL. Elevated FSH suggests primary gonadal failure, menopause, or premature ovarian failure. Low FSH indicates pituitary insufficiency or hypothalamic dysfunction. Chemiluminescent immunoassay provides high sensitivity. FSH:LH ratio helps evaluate reproductive disorders. Used in infertility workup, puberty assessment, and menopause confirmation. Critical for assessing ovarian reserve and predicting response to fertility treatments.
